title: 0 to 100 or 41 to 96? Range Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
A maths test is marked out of 100, so any mark from 0 to 100 is allowed. But the class only scored from 41 to 96. Which is the real answer? Both, and maths gives them two different names: the codomain and the range. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we meet the domain, the codomain and the range of a function.

You will watch a function run live, one arrow at a time, from A to B, and see which elements of the codomain are hit and which are never hit. We meet the words image and preimage, compare the codomain with the range side by side, and then watch the graph of x squared as a parameter a grows, with the domain stretching on the x axis and the range climbing on the y axis. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with f(x) = x squared + 1, the exam trap of using only the end points, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Allowed marks vs scored marks
0:30 Domain, codomain and range
1:00 Live: a function runs from A to B
1:32 Image and preimage
1:49 Codomain vs range: side by side
2:38 Live graph: watch the range grow
3:27 Worked example: f(x) = x squared + 1
4:09 Exam trap: do not use only the end points
4:30 Where it is asked
4:40 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:21 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 18): Real-Valued Functions. Diya's body temperature gives one number for every hour of the day. What kind of function is that?
